correctness.rationale: At a differentiability angle every supporting point has the same normal coordinate h and tangential coordinate h′ (use the supporting-point inequalities at angular increments of both signs). The line separation is therefore |h₁′−h₂′|. The defining half-integral, absolute continuity, and the four quadrants give 2 TV(H) with H the square-root support difference in u=cos²θ. The sign of 2H′ is the sign of A²d²−C²b²+AC(A−C)u because the compared terms are nonnegative; its endpoint factors are (Ad−Cb)(Ad+Cb) and (Ac−Ca)(Ac+Ca). This proves monotonicity even at an endpoint equality or for circles, and exactly one strict interior extremum when the signs differ. At the stationary point the support values have ratio A/C; substitution yields the stated signed radical and the strict increase over twice the absolute endpoint gap. The nested example gives u*=11/30 and H(u*)²=14/15, with both endpoint values 1. The general zero-distance criterion follows from a constant support difference and additivity under disk offsets. The supplied checker was inspected, not run, and angular quadrature is not the proof.
residual_risks: Formula requires shared center, principal directions and alignment of the major axes. General kernel statement is for compact convex bodies with the prescribed oriented normal pairing.
